part.text:
Fixed. The issue was that `RuntimeMetrics::num_blocking_threads()` double-counted worker threads, because multi-threaded runtime workers are spawned through the blocking pool via `spawn_blocking` (tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread/worker.rs:447), inflating the pool's `num_threads` counter.

Changes:
- `tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread/handle/metrics.rs`: `num_blocking_threads()` now does `blocking_threads.saturating_sub(self.num_workers())`.
- `tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread_alt/handle/metrics.rs`: same fix — `blocking_spawner.num_threads().saturating_sub(self.num_workers())`.

Validation: `cargo test -p tokio --test rt_metrics --features full` with `--cfg tokio_unstable` — `num_blocking_threads`, `num_idle_blocking_threads`, and all other metrics tests pass (20/22). The only 2 failures are `io_driver_fd_count`/`io_driver_ready_count`, which fail solely because the container has no network access (they connect to `google.com:80`) and are unrelated to this change. All 138 `--lib` tests also pass.
